builder.setup:
<%= pb_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.text_field :email, props: { label: "Email", required: true } %>
<% end %>
builder.formWith:
<%= form_with model: @user, builder: Playbook::Forms::Builder do |f| %>
  <%= f.text_field :email, props: { label: "Email" } %>
<% end %>
builder.validation: pb_form_with defaults validate to false. validate: true sets data-pb-form-validation for Playbook client validation. PbFormValidation finds the field kit via a *_kit classname, or via data-pb-dropdown / data-pb-multi-level-select for those kits. It binds invalid in capture on the form (not a one-time [required] snapshot) so controls that toggle required after mount still get data-message. Server/model validation remains the host application responsibility. Most builder fields also map record.errors into props.error unless the caller sets error explicitly (including nil).
builder.lifecycle: pb_form_with invokes formHelper when available. PbFormValidation is registered with PbKitRegistry; its MutationObserver handles dynamically added forms, including Turbo navigation. Load the Playbook Rails bundle in the host.
builder.simpleForm: No Simple Form adapter is declared by this contract. These methods belong to Playbook::Forms::Builder.

methods.name: email_field

binding.name: The Rails helper derives the input name from the builder object name and attribute, including nested form scopes.
binding.value: The Rails helper uses the model value unless overridden; explicit props.value is forwarded as the HTML value option. There is no builder defaultValue argument.

submission.value: The current Rails-generated input or textarea value under the model-scoped name.

htmlOptions.description: Pass HTML attributes as builder keyword arguments, outside props, or in props.input_options. The Rails helper renders the input and receives both.
htmlOptions.overrides: The builder sets placeholder from props (default empty), forwards props.required when true, and forwards explicit props.type, value, disabled, autocomplete, mask and validation. props.input_options is merged last, so it overrides those and the keyword options: input_options.classname is appended to class, input_options.data is merged key by key, and a literal input_options.class is ignored. It derives props.input_options.id from the rendered input.

methods.name: dropdown_field

binding.name: The name argument is assigned directly to props.name. Pass the model attribute (e.g. :country) so auto-bound values and errors can read @object; supply user[country] explicitly when you need a nested parameter name instead.
binding.value: Unless props.default_value is set, the builder reads the model attribute and resolves it against props.options to an option hash (or array of hashes for multi_select). Unmatched ids are left unset; bare ids are never passed through.

htmlOptions.description: This method accepts props only, not arbitrary HTML keyword arguments.

block.description: This builder method does not forward a caller block to the kit.

submission.value: Selected option id in a CSS-hidden input (not input type=hidden).
submission.multi: syncHiddenInputs emits one hidden input per selected id in selection order, adds [] to the name only if absent and clears the original CSS-hidden input and removes its name while selections exist, so no blank array entry is submitted. When empty, the original name and required state are restored, including after Turbo reconnects. These submission fixes apply whether or not allow_option_creation is enabled. With enable_pill_reorder, drag or keyboard reordering updates that same selection order before syncHiddenInputs runs, so submitted values and pb:dropdown:reordered / pb:dropdown:selected details match the pill order. Comma-joining is used for default-value encoding, not as an additional submitted selection.
submission.dynamicOptions: props.options_by_context with props.context_selector replaces the rendered options when the referenced element fires change, and props.clear_on_context_change (default true) then clears the selection, so a context change can submit an empty value. A pb:dropdown:updateOptions event, or an event named in props.options_event_type, replaces options the same way; clearSelection: false keeps only selections whose id exists in the replacement options.

validation.required: props.required sets required on the CSS-hidden input. Do not assume a focusable native validation UI.

error.example: Omit props.error, or pass an explicit message / nil to override
error.description: Unless props.error is set (including explicit nil), the builder sets it from record.errors.full_messages_for(attribute).first when present.

validation.client: props.validation_message becomes data-message on the CSS-hidden input (single and multi-select).

methods.example:
<%= pb_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.dropdown_field :country, props: { label: "Country", options: [{ id: "ca", value: "canada", label: "Canada" }], required: true, validation_message: "Please select a country" } %>
<% end %>

validation.required: props.required is passed to the nested text_input.

error.example: Omit props.error, or pass an explicit message / nil to override
error.description: Unless props.error is set (including explicit nil), the builder sets it from record.errors.full_messages_for(attribute).first when present.

validation.client: props.validation_message becomes the nested text_input validation.message.

methods.example:
<%= pb_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.time_picker :appointment_time, props: { label: true, required: true } %>
<% end %>

methods.name: typeahead

binding.name: The name argument is assigned directly to props.name. Pass the model attribute (e.g. :country) so auto-bound values and errors can read @object; supply user[country] explicitly when you need a nested parameter name instead.
binding.value: Unless props.default_options is set, the builder auto-binds only when the model attribute is already option-shaped ({label,value} or an array of those). A bare id still needs explicit default_options.

htmlOptions.description: The positional _options and _html_options are ignored. input_options.id defaults to name_input. Other input_options behavior depends on the native/React rendering branch.

block.description: This builder method does not forward a caller block to the kit.

submission.value: Depends on the rendering branch. Native Rails renders a named search text_input; the React-backed branch delegates selection submission to Typeahead.

multi.description: No uniform array serialization contract is declared here across both rendering branches.

validation.required: props.required is handled by the kit rendering branch.

error.example: Omit props.error, or pass an explicit message / nil to override
error.description: Auto-mapped or explicit error is set on props. The React-backed branch receives it; the native Rails template does not forward error to its nested text_input.

validation.client: props.validation.message is copied to input_options.data.validation_message; the kit also receives validation.

methods.example:
<%= pb_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.typeahead :country, props: { label: "Country", is_multi: false, options: [{ label: "Canada", value: "ca" }], required: true } %>
<% end %>

actions.description: Yields an ActionArea inside ol.pb-form-actions. submit defaults props.type to submit and props.text to the supplied value or Rails submit_default_value. button renders supplied props in an li.

questions: Can I use this kit in a Rails form?
How do I use pb_form_with or form_with?
faqs.answer: Use Playbook-owned pb_form_with, or form_with with builder: Playbook::Forms::Builder. See the listed methods and examples for this kit. Builder arguments are a separate API from standalone kit props.

questions: How do I show ActiveRecord errors?
How do I enable client validation?
How do I set a custom required-field message?
faqs.answer: Most builder fields auto-map record.errors.full_messages_for(attribute) into props.error unless error is set explicitly (including nil to opt out). Checkbox still needs an explicit boolean error flag, and StarRating has no error prop. A required indicator is visual only. pb_form_with validate: true enables Playbook client validation; it does not run model validations. Custom required messages use props.validation.message on text-style fields (including text_area and telephone_field) and props.validation_message on selection-style fields (select, dropdown_field, check_box, phone_number_field, star_rating_field, multi_level_select, and similar). Phone kits own their UI and use validation_message for the empty required copy only.

questions: Does the builder read the model value?
faqs.answer: Check the method binding and submission fields. With a bound model, most fields auto-populate values (default_date, default_value, selected_ids, default_options, etc.) unless those props are set. Rails-helper wrappers use model-scoped names; direct kit wrappers assign the name argument to props.name verbatim—pass the attribute for auto-bind, or a nested string like user[country] when you need that parameter shape.

questions: Where do name id required maxlength min step autocomplete and data attributes go?
What can I put in input_options?
faqs.answer: Use the method htmlOptions contract. Text field wrappers accept HTML keyword arguments outside props; select wrappers accept positional html_options. Direct wrappers generally accept only props. Text field wrappers and check_box also merge props.input_options into the Rails-generated field; other methods do not.

questions: Does pb_form_with initialize after Turbo navigation?
Do I need a Stimulus controller to initialize the form?
faqs.answer: pb_form_with invokes formHelper when available, and Playbook registers PbFormValidation with PbKitRegistry for dynamically added forms. This requires the Playbook Rails bundle. No host-specific Stimulus controller is part of this contract.

questions: Can I use these methods with Simple Form?
faqs.answer: The documented methods belong to Playbook::Forms::Builder. This metadata does not declare a Simple Form adapter; host integrations must be documented separately.
